EVERYONE MATTERS, EVERYONE CARES
THE ORCHARD SCHOOL
The Orchard School is a Foundation Special School. We cater for 116 pupils who have behaviour and learning difficulties as identified by their Education Health and Care Plans (EHC Plans).
Our school caters for primary and secondary aged pupils in three separate phases.
Staff at The Orchard are skilled in working with pupils who have a range of difficulties that prevent them from accessing their learning.

9 July 2026
Free Kellogg's breakfast for families at Morrisons cafes Between 29th June and 6th September 2026, families can access free Kellogg's breakfasts in all Morrisons Cafes. This is available to both children and adults , who can choose from much-loved favourites Corn Flakes or Rice Krispies, topped with their choice of dairy or non-dairy milk and a free apple or banana. In addition to the Kellogg's Breakfast offer, Morrisons 'Kids Eat Free' offer will continue to run in all its Cafés, allowing families to enjoy a free meal and drink for one child aged 16 or under when they purchase an adult main meal costing over £5 from The Breakfasts and The Classics menu.
25 June 2026
Dear Parents and Carers, Due to the exceptionally high temperatures experienced throughout this week, and with further extreme heat forecast for Friday 26 June 2026, we have made the difficult decision to close The Orchard School early, with all pupils finishing at 12.30pm. Whilst our classrooms are air conditioned and provide a comfortable learning environment, our pupils have very limited opportunities to regulate outside of the classroom. Unfortunately, our school field remains out of bounds due to the extreme weather conditions, significantly reducing access to the outdoor spaces that many of our pupils rely on to support their social, emotional and mental wellbeing. As a specialist SEMH school, we know that maintaining access to appropriate regulation spaces is essential. Having carefully considered the forecast temperatures and the impact of the prolonged heat on our pupils and staff, we believe that an early finish is the safest and most appropriate course of action. Parents and carers who usually collect their child from school are asked to do so at 12.30 pm. The school office will contact our transport providers to ensure that taxi collections are rearranged for 12.30 pm wherever applicable. We appreciate that this decision may cause inconvenience and thank you for your understanding and support. If you anticipate any difficulties with the revised collection time, please contact the school office as soon as possible so that we can discuss appropriate arrangements. Thank you for your continued support as we work to keep everyone in our school community safe during this period of extreme weather.

Dear Parents and Carers, We would like to say a warm and heartfelt thank you to all our incredibly supportive, kind, and generous parents and carers who donated cakes, biscuits, and treats for our Comic Relief Bake Sale , as well as giving your children money to buy something on the day! Your enthusiasm, kindness, and willingness to help made the event a real success. Thanks to your amazing contributions, we raised an impressive £140 for Comic Relief! We are so grateful for your continued support. Events like this simply wouldn't be possible without you, and your generosity helps us teach our pupils the importance of community, kindness, and giving back. Thank you for making such a positive difference. Warmest wishes and appreciation The Orchard School
19 March 2026
We have made the difficult decision to postpone our upcoming Easter Egg Run. This is always a much-loved event in our school community, and we are incredibly grateful to the biker group for their continued kindness, generosity and support each year. We are already looking ahead to rearranging the event for later in the term, so that it can take place in a safe, well-planned, and enjoyable way for everyone. Thank you to our families, staff and wider community for your understanding and ongoing support. We look forward to bringing everyone together soon.
16 March 2026
Dear Parents and Carers, We would like to let families know about a lovely community event taking place at The Orchard School this Sunday, 22 March. The Whitstable Toy Run Association (WTRA) will once again be visiting the school as part of their annual Easter Egg Run. Riders will set off from Tankerton at 12:00 and are expected to arrive at The Orchard School at approximately 15:00. The group ride motorcycles through the area collecting and delivering Easter eggs to schools and charities. It is a wonderful act of generosity and community spirit. Last year the riders donated over 450 Easter eggs, which were shared between our pupils, St Nicholas Special School and local food banks. Their support makes a real difference to many families. Weather permitting, families who are nearby are very welcome to come along and help us show appreciation and say thank you to the riders who give up their time to support local children and charities. We are incredibly grateful to the Whitstable Toy Run Association and all the riders who take part. Their kindness and commitment to supporting the community is something we are proud to be part of. Finally, many of you will know that our recent Ofsted inspection report will be published soon. The new national framework no longer gives overall graded judgements. Instead it provides detailed feedback about the school's strengths and areas for development. We look forward to sharing the report with families and continuing the positive journey we are on together at The Orchard. Thank you, as always, for your continued support.

Personalised Learning & EHCPS
Meeting individual needs. Unlocking potential.
Every pupil at The Orchard School has an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP). These plans form the foundation of our personalised approach — guiding the way we teach, support and nurture each young person across their time with us.
We don’t believe in one-size-fits-all. Instead, we create responsive, relational learning journeys that reflect each pupil’s strengths, interests and needs — always with their EHCP outcomes at the centre.
What Personalised Learning Looks Like:
EHCPs Drive Our Provision
Pupil Voice Matters
Pupils are involved in setting their own targets and reflecting on what helps them learn best. Whether through conversation, visuals or key adult support, their views help shape their journey.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Orchard School - Outdoor Learning & Enrichment
pageCache.text:
Outdoor Learning & Enrichment
New experiences. Safe challenges. Lasting confidence.
At The Orchard School, outdoor learning and enrichment are not extras-they are essential. For many of our pupils, success and self-belief begin beyond the classroom. That’s why we provide regular, structured opportunities to learn through movement, nature, creativity and challenge.
These experiences help pupils to develop resilience, build relationships, regulate emotions and grow in confidence. Whether it’s learning to cook over a fire, exploring local woodland, or visiting a museum for the first time, we create safe but meaningful opportunities to take risks, succeed and shine.
Our Offer Includes:
Gardening, conservation and seasonal projects
PE, team games and structured physical activity
Creative workshops, visiting artists and specialist sessions
Forest School and Outdoor Learning Development
As part of our ongoing 3-year site improvement project, we are developing a dedicated Forest School and Outdoor Learning space within our grounds. This area is being designed to meet individual pupil needs, offering calm, sensory-rich environments that nurture curiosity and connection with nature. Once complete, it will include learning shelters, fire and tool areas, and spaces for creative, therapeutic and environmental learning.
This development forms a key part of our outdoor learning curriculum – supporting regulation, wellbeing and readiness to learn through hands-on exploration and safe challenges in nature.
Why It Matters:
Promotes sensory regulation and positive mental health
Builds social skills, independence and curiosity
Strengthens staff–pupil relationships through shared experiences
Encourages risk-taking in a safe, supported way
Pupil Voice Leads the Way
We listen to what pupils enjoy, want to try, and feel ready for-shaping activities around their interests and emotional needs. Where appropriate, enrichment is used as part of EHCP targets, therapeutic goals or attendance reintegration plans.

Assessment & Progress
Measuring what matters. Celebrating the whole child.
At The Orchard School, we believe that progress is personal. For pupils with SEMH needs, success is not only academic — it includes emotional regulation, independence, communication, and social confidence. That’s why our approach to assessment is broad, balanced and meaningful.
We track each pupil’s journey closely to understand what’s working, identify next steps, and celebrate progress in all its forms.
Our Approach to Assessment
Aligned with EHCP outcomes and therapeutic priorities
Shared regularly with families and professionals
What We Assess
Key Features
Reporting to Families
We value open dialogue with families and professionals. Progress is shared regularly through:
Termly reports or review meetings
EHCP annual reviews
Informal check-ins, phone calls and shared celebrations

pageCache.pageTitle: The Orchard School - PSHE and RHSE
pageCache.text:
PSHE and RHSE
Personal development rooted in trust, safety and emotional growth.
At The Orchard School, Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) education is more than a subject — it’s woven into the fabric of school life. For pupils with SEMH needs, understanding themselves, building safe relationships, and navigating the wider world is fundamental to lifelong wellbeing.
We deliver a carefully planned PSHE curriculum across both the Primary and Secondary Phases, tailored to our pupils’ developmental needs, EHCP outcomes, and lived experiences.
Our PSHE Curriculum Focuses On:
Emotional regulation and self-awareness
Mental health and wellbeing
Friendships and social skills
Managing feelings and building resilience
Safety, risk and personal boundaries
Belonging, identity and diversity
Preparing for adulthood and independence
Relationships, Sex and Health Education (RSHE)
RSHE is a statutory part of our wider PSHE offer and is delivered in a way that is safe, age-appropriate, and emotionally sensitive.
Progression Across Key Stages
Key Stage 2 (Primary)
Focus: Relationships Education and Health Education
Key Stage 3 (Lower Secondary)
Focus: Relationships and Sex Education & Health Education
Key Stage 4 (Upper Secondary)
Focus: Advanced RSE & Personal Development
Families and people who care for me
Friendships and respect
Online safety
Mental wellbeing
Developing healthy relationships (respect, consent, peer pressure)
Online and media influence
Mental health and coping strategies
Healthy intimate relationships (consent, respect, avoiding exploitation)
How We Teach PSHE & RSHE
Working in Partnership
We work closely with families and offer clear information about curriculum content and delivery. Parents have the right to request withdrawal from specific elements of sex education in line with statutory guidance.
If you would like to read our full RSE policy or have any questions about the content, please contact Mr McFarnell (Assistant Headteacher) via the school office. We welcome parent engagement and are happy to discuss how we deliver these topics in a way that supports your child’s needs.

PE and Sport Premium (Primary)
Confidence. Movement. Connection.
At The Orchard School, we use the PE and Sport Premium to support physical development, emotional regulation and social interaction for our Primary Phase pupils. For children with SEMH needs, movement isn’t just about fitness — it’s about freedom, confidence and joy.
Our offer is inclusive, therapeutic and designed to build healthy habits that last a lifetime.
What Is PE and Sport Premium?
PE and Sport Premium is government funding given to primary schools to improve the quality of PE and sport provision. It helps schools broaden access, increase engagement, and promote healthy lifestyles.
How We Use Our Funding
Our SEMH-focused approach uses the funding to:
Deliver high-quality PE lessons across Primary
Provide specialist sports coaching and enrichment activities
Why It Matters
Builds motor skills, coordination and stamina
Supports emotional regulation and sensory integration
Encourages teamwork, communication and resilience
Promotes enjoyment of activity — not competition
Accountability & Reporting
We publish our PE and Sport Premium Strategy and Spending Overview annually.

SEND Information Report
Inclusive. Individualised. Rooted in care.
The Orchard School is a specialist provision for pupils with social, emotional and mental health (SEMH) needs. All of our pupils have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP), and our approach is designed to meet complex needs through therapeutic support, relational practice and inclusive teaching.
This SEND Information Report outlines how we identify, support and review the needs of our learners-and how we work in partnership with families and professionals to help each child succeed.
What We Offer
Our curriculum, routines and relationships are all shaped to support pupils with:
All provision is informed by Therapeutic Thinking, and guided by our Mission, Vision and Values: Everyone Matters. Everyone Cares.
Social, emotional and mental health needs (SEMH)
Co-occurring neurodivergence (e.g. ADHD, ASC)
Speech, language and communication needs
Sensory processing differences
Experiences of trauma, attachment or relational disruption
Complex behaviour linked to emotional regulation
How We Support SEND
Small class sizes with high staff-to-pupil ratios
Working in Partnership with Families
We believe families are key to pupil progress.

Careers Education Information, Advice and Guidance (CEIAG) at The Orchard School
At The Orchard School, Everyone Matters, Everyone Cares. Our approach to Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance (CEIAG) ensures every pupil is supported to explore their interests, build confidence and make positive, informed choices about their future.
How We Measure Impact
We use national frameworks and pupil feedback to make sure our careers programme makes a real difference. This includes: • Ongoing evaluation against the eight Gatsby Benchmarks using Compass+. • A termly-reviewed Careers Plan that tracks priorities and outcomes for our pupils. • Feedback from pupils, parents, staff, employers and CEIAG partners. • Monitoring of destinations, ensuring each young person moves on to education, training or employment that is right for them.
We regularly review and refine our careers provision so that it stays inclusive, aspirational and personalised. Through The Orchard Way, we aim to help every young person discover their strengths, understand the world of work and feel proud of the next step in their journey.
